issues.title: Diagnostic message leaks into stdout with --result-only when using --sql @file

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot query https://books.toscrape.com/ --sql @.test-sessions/extract_books.sql --result-only
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Only the JSON array of results on stdout, no other text.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The line "Finding browser4 root from "/home/vincent/workspace/Browser4-4.12"" appears on stdout before the JSON array. This contaminates machine-readable output and would break JSON parsers.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The file-path resolution logic (likely in the CLI's argument parsing for `@file` syntax) prints a diagnostic to stdout before the query executes. The `--result-only` flag appears to filter only the server response envelope, not earlier CLI-level diagnostic output. The file resolution happens before the HTTP request is made, so it's outside the scope of the server-side response filtering.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — likely in the argument parsing or SQL file loading path where `@file` paths are resolved and the "Finding browser4 root" message is printed.
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Move the "Finding browser4 root" message to stderr instead of stdout
- In `--result-only` mode, suppress all non-result stdout, including CLI-level diagnostics
- Consider printing this diagnostic only in verbose/debug mode, or only when the root cannot be found automatically

issues.title: Inline --sql quoting requires escaping single quotes on Linux/bash, risking shell errors

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot query URL --sql "SELECT DOM_FIRST_TEXT(DOM, 'h3 a') AS title FROM DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, 'article.product_pod')"
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The command should work without complex escaping, or the documentation should clearly show the exact escaping pattern needed for Linux/bash with single-quoted CSS selectors inside double-quoted SQL.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The command works but the CLI internally re-escapes the single quotes (visible in the debug output showing `'\''h3 a'\''`). This fragile escaping could easily break with different shells or more complex queries. The SKILL.md warns about this on Windows but the issue affects Linux/bash too.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The `./b4w.ps1` wrapper passes arguments through PowerShell which has its own quoting rules. When the outer SQL uses double quotes and CSS selectors use single quotes, the shell and PowerShell layers interact in ways that require careful escaping. This is inherent to mixing shell quoting with PowerShell argument passing.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add a Linux/bash-specific warning in the shell-quoting reference alongside the existing Windows warning
- Show a concrete Linux/bash example with single-quote escaping in the X-SQL quick-start section
- Recommend `--sql @file` or `--sql-stdin` as the primary methods even on Linux when CSS selectors contain quotes
- Consider adding `--sql-stdin` as the first recommended method in the SKILL.md decision tree
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: htmlsnapshot inspect does not directly suggest CSS selector for title text inside h3 > a

sections.body: 1. ./b4w.ps1 goto http://books.toscrape.com/ 2. ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot 3. ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot inspect
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The inspect output should suggest a text-extraction selector for the book title, such as "h3 a" or "h3", in the "Suggested selectors" list alongside the price selector `p.price_color`.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The inspect output shows `h3:expr(a>0)` as a suggested selector (a PowerCSS structural selector), and the sample structure shows the h3 element with text. But unlike `p.price_color` which directly shows sample values ("£51.77" | "£53.74" | "£50.10"), there is no explicit text-extraction selector suggestion like "h3 a" showing sample title values. The user must infer from the sample structure that `h3` contains the title text.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The `htmlsnapshot inspect` text-discovery logic detects text-bearing elements with PowerCSS expression selectors but does not generate explicit text-extraction selector suggestions in the same format as it does for other element types. The sample values are shown in the tree structure but not in the suggested selectors table for non-price-like patterns. Investigation needed to understand why `p.price_color` gets sample values shown but `h3 a` does not.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add text-extraction selector suggestions with sample values for heading/name/title patterns, similar to how price selectors are shown
- Show sample text values in the suggested selectors table for any text-bearing element, not just price-like elements
- Consider a dedicated "Text selectors" section in the inspect output showing the best selector for visible text content
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: The @url placeholder relationship to the positional URL argument is undocumented in CLI help

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot query --help
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The help output for `htmlsnapshot query` should explain that the URL passed as a positional argument replaces `@url` in the X-SQL query, and that `@url` is the recommended placeholder.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The help output for `htmlsnapshot query` (and the main help) does not mention the `@url` placeholder or how it relates to the URL argument. This information is only available in the x-sql.md reference file, which a new user may not know to consult.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The `@url` placeholder is a server-side SQL template feature. The CLI help is generated from command definitions that don't include this level of detail about X-SQL placeholder semantics.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add a brief note in `htmlsnapshot query --help` explaining that `@url` in the query is replaced by the URL argument
- Add a short example in the help showing `SELECT ... FROM DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, ...)`
- Include `@url` documentation in the `--help extract` category output
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: htmlsnapshot inspect suggested selectors include PowerCSS expressions without explanation of what :expr() selectors are

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot inspect
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: When `:expr()` selectors appear in the suggested selectors list, there should be a brief explanatory note or a link to the PowerCSS documentation.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Selectors like `a:expr(img>0)`, `img:expr(img>0)`, `h3:expr(a>0)`, `article:expr(img>0)`, `div:expr(img>0)` appear without any explanation of what the `:expr()` syntax means. A new user encountering these for the first time would not understand that `:expr(img>0)` means "elements that have at least one descendant ".
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The inspect output is auto-generated from CSS selector discovery. PowerCSS `:expr()` selectors are generated when structural features are more discriminative than class/id selectors, but no contextual explanation is included in the output.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add a one-line legend or footnote in the inspect output explaining the `:expr()` syntax
- Link to the PowerCSS reference in a tip after the inspect output when PowerCSS selectors appear
- Show the meaning of each `:expr()` selector in a human-readable form (e.g., "a:expr(img>0) → links containing images")
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Book titles are truncated in X-SQL results (ellipsis in output)

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot query URL --sql @extract_books.sql
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Full book titles should be returned without truncation.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Several titles are truncated with "..." in the output: e.g., "A Light in the ..." (full title: "A Light in the Attic"), "Sapiens: A Brief History ..." (full: "Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind").
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The truncation likely occurs in the DOM text extraction or the H2 database's text column width defaults. The `DOM_FIRST_TEXT` function or the result serialization may apply a character limit. Alternatively, this could be the actual text content rendered on the page (CSS text-overflow: ellipsis).
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Investigate whether truncation happens at the DOM level (page rendering), text extraction level, or result serialization level
- If at the extraction level, increase the default text length limit or add a parameter to control it
- If the page itself truncates with CSS, document this as a known limitation and suggest using `DOM_FIRST_ATTR(DOM, 'a', 'title')` as a workaround for truncated link text
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: No --help output category for 'query' or 'htmlsnapshot' subcommand group

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 --help query  OR  ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot query --help
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Category-based help should include an 'extract' or 'query' category that covers htmlsnapshot query, and `htmlsnapshot query --help` should show query-specific options like --sql, --sql-stdin, --sql-base64, --result-only.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The `--help extract` category exists and does mention htmlsnapshot. However, running `htmlsnapshot query --help` only shows generic `htmlsnapshot` help, not query-specific options. The `--sql` and `--result-only` flags are not visible without reading the x-sql.md reference.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: `htmlsnapshot query` is a subcommand of `htmlsnapshot`, and the help system may not generate per-subcommand help pages. The `--sql` flag may be defined at the `htmlsnapshot` level but only applicable to the `query` subcommand.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add `htmlsnapshot query --help` support showing query-specific flags (--sql, --sql-stdin, --sql-base64, --result-only)
- Include a brief X-SQL example in the htmlsnapshot query help output
- Add a dedicated --help category for 'query' or 'x-sql'
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
